clue.text: Like blooms left by the girl at Bly

parts.note: Flora is the little girl at Bly in Henry James's The Turn of the Screw

explanation.surface: A description of flowers left behind by a child in a Victorian ghost story.
explanation.definitionFit: Something floral resembles or consists of flowers, the way blooms do.

clue.text: Writer born in the US capital

definitions.meaning: Jack ..., author of The Call of the Wild, was born in San Francisco
the capital city of England and the United Kingdom

explanation.definitionFit: Jack London was an American novelist, and the English capital shares his surname.

clue.text: Borrow gypsy gentleman's whiskey

definitions.meaning: The Romany word for a gentleman
a whiskey distilled from ... grain, popular in North America

explanation.surface: A gentleman of the road cadges a glass of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is both Borrow's Romany term for a gentleman and a kind of grain spirit.

clue.text: Modern Gods author, Irish youth has embraced

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside, so the youth word wraps around the Irish abbreviation

parts.note: a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A young Irishman hugs the writer of a recent novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Laird, the Northern Irish poet and novelist, wrote the novel Modern Gods.

clue.text: Spiel by Geordie egoist, Willoughby

parts.note: patter is glib persuasive talk, a spiel
a Geordie is from Newcastle in the north-east of England, NE

explanation.surface: A Tyneside self-admirer delivers his sales pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a native of Tyneside, in north-east England, so NE. The puzzle file prints the answer with a final S, but the wordplay and definition both give PATTERNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Willoughby Patterne is the vain hero of George Meredith's novel The Egoist.

clue.text: Poet with no hot water in France's upland area

indicators.note: says a letter is dropped from the poet's surname

parts.note: Sylvia Plath, the American poet
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
eau is the French word for water

explanation.surface: A poet takes cold water on a French holiday in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes H from PLATH to leave PLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a raised stretch of flat high ground, an elevated tableland.

clue.text: A sum raised in America for St Jude

indicators.note: the letters before it are placed inside the word for America

parts.note: America is often called the US

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the sum word is turned round

parts.note: to add is to sum, total up

explanation.surface: A sum of money collected in the United States for a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America' is taken as THE US, and the saint is Jude's other gospel name, so the surface's charity collection is a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Jude the apostle is also known as Thaddaeus in the gospels of Mark and Matthew.

clue.text: Dodgy men loiter by an authoress

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Suspicious men hang around near a woman writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Wuthering Heights was a female novelist, which authoress denotes.

clue.text: Book new rooms to rent

indicators.note: rent here is the past tense of rend, meaning torn apart, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An advertisement for fresh accommodation available to let.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like letting rooms, but means torn: it rearranges ROOMSTO into OSTROMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostromo is a novel by Joseph Conrad, so a book.

clue.text: Part of a cake she's offered as a tournament prize

definitions.meaning: candied stems of a herb used to decorate cakes

definitions.text: she's offered as a tournament prize
definitions.meaning: the princess in Ariosto's Orlando Furioso promised as a prize to the victor

explanation.definitionFit: Candied angelica tops cakes, and Ariosto's heroine Angelica is held out as a reward to champions.

clue.text: Like a song of love in spring

indicators.note: the letter for love is placed inside the word for spring

parts.note: to spring up is to arise
love is nil in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A love song sung in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariose means melodious, having the character of an aria or air.

clue.text: For Catherine, her beheading sounded novel

definitions.text: For Catherine, her beheading sounded novel

parts.words: For Catherine, her beheading sounded novel
parts.note: Catherine Howard, Henry VIII's fifth wife, met her end on the block, and that phrase, said with the possessive, is the title of an E M Forster novel

explanation.surface: The execution of a Tudor queen came as a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The fate of Henry VIII's queen Catherine and Forster's novel share the same words.

clue.text: Like a Spartan doubter, heartlessly taken in by a friend

indicators.note: the trimmed doubter word is held inside the article and friend words

parts.note: an ally is a friend

indicators.note: says the middle letter of the doubter word is removed

parts.note: a sceptic doubts

explanation.surface: A suspicious person, deceived by a pal, takes it like a stoic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like a Spartan' fits because ancient Sparta was proverbial for austerity; 'taken in by' looks like deception but signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartans were famed for austere self-denial, which is how an ascetic lives.

clue.text: Made glorious summer by this son of —" (Richard III)

definitions.text: Made glorious summer by this son of —" (Richard III)

parts.words: Made glorious summer by this son of —" (Richard III)
parts.note: the opening of Shakespeare's Richard III: 'Now is the winter of our discontent / Made glorious summer by this sun of ...', with a pun on son and sun

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line names the royal house whose son, Edward IV, ended the winter of discontent.

clue.text: Redcoat's mum misrepresented by a period piece

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word, with its S

explanation.surface: A soldier's mother is portrayed falsely in a historical film.
explanation.definitionFit: A play or film set in an earlier era, with historical clothes, is a period piece.

clue.text: Patience perhaps shown by people in circus act

parts.note: Patience Strong was a popular English writer of sentimental verse
man means humankind, people

explanation.surface: Patience is shown by those who perform in a circus.
explanation.walkthrough: Patience Strong was a British author of greeting-card style poems. 'perhaps' marks her as one example of someone with that surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A man performing feats of strength is a classic circus act.

clue.text: Hook may run riot around a port

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the a
to run riot is to go wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Captain Hook may go on the rampage near a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run riot' rearranges HOOKMAY into YOKOHM, and 'around' places it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Yokohama is a major seaport in Japan, near Tokyo.

clue.text: Spike and two altos, regularly playing for a crime reporter

parts.note: to spike a drink is to doctor it

indicators.note: every other letter is taken from the two words

parts.note: on means playing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: A musician named Spike and two alto singers perform together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of TWO ALTOS, giving WATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Watson narrates Sherlock Holmes's cases, so he reports on crimes.

clue.text: A command spoken by a Roman general

indicators.note: spoken says the words are said aloud

parts.note: a strong grip on things, command; one who has it is a gripper

explanation.surface: An order given out loud by a Roman soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was Augustus's general, victor at Actium.

clue.text: Tale about Saville finally produces a Booker winner

indicators.note: the tale word is placed round the letter

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A story about a novel's ending wins a literary prize.
explanation.walkthrough: David Storey won the Booker Prize in 1976 with Saville, which gives the surface its sense.
explanation.definitionFit: David Storey won the 1976 Booker Prize, so he is a Booker winner.

clue.text: Ring worn round the neck of Tolkien's lead monster

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an orc is a monster, as in Tolkien's own books

explanation.surface: A ring worn by Tolkien's chief orc.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a Celtic metal neck ring or collar.

clue.text: Thor for example, seen tidy or dishevelled

indicators.note: dishevelled means untidy, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: The god of thunder appears either neat or scruffy.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is a god of the Scandinavian pantheon, one example of a Viking god.

clue.text: Soames, he sold his soul, some have no choice

indicators.note: some of the letters are taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man sold his soul to the devil, and some people have no option.
explanation.walkthrough: Enoch Soames, in Max Beerbohm's story, sells his soul to see his future fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Beerbohm's poet who sells his soul has the forename Enoch.

clue.text: Camp actor grasping fully the subject of In Memoriam

indicators.note: the actor word holds the fully word inside it

parts.note: a ham is an overacting performer
all means fully, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A flamboyant actor clutches a memorial poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson wrote In Memoriam A.H.H. to mourn his friend Arthur Hallam.

clue.text: Duke kicked out after boom is over

parts.note: to boom is to thrive, prosper
O is the abbreviation for over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A duke is deposed after his boom years end.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Tempest, Prospero is the rightful Duke of Milan, ousted by his brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's magician in The Tempest is the deposed Duke of Milan.

clue.text: Writer, gaping, scratching head

indicators.note: scratching means removing, so the first letter goes

parts.note: gaping means open

explanation.surface: A writer stares open-mouthed, scratching his head.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is the instrument a writer uses, and pen also means to write.

clue.text: Novel song about 500 articles back to back

indicators.note: the song word goes around the Roman numeral

parts.note: a lay is a song
D is the Roman numeral for 500
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: two copies placed back to back, the second turned round

parts.note: the second article, also an

explanation.surface: A new song about five hundred items arranged one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Anna is a novel by Anthony Trollope.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Anna is a Trollope novel, so a novel.

clue.text: Play female rugby sides beginning in Vienna

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters
the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A women's rugby team kicks off in Vienna.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's history about Agincourt is a play.
